neighbours.label: words inside lines of rhymed verse (poetry set out line by line)
fire:
The shepherd led his flock along,
And sang a merry country song,
Until the evening star was up.

When winter winds blow cold and grey,
The children run indoors to play,
And mother lights the lamp.

I wandered down the silent lane,
And heard the whisper of the rain
Upon the cottage roof.

The sailor dreams of home and hearth,
Of daisies on the greening earth,
And bread upon the board.

O little bird upon the bough,
Why do you sing so sweetly now,
When all the woods are bare?

The maidens dance upon the lea,
Beneath the spreading willow tree,
Till dusk has called them home.

And when the bells of evening ring,
The weary ploughmen rest and sing
Of harvests long ago.

My heart is like a frozen stream,
That waits beneath the moon's pale beam
For spring to set it free.
quiet: The shepherd led his flock along the road and sang a country song until the evening star rose.
When the winter winds are cold, the children stay indoors to play while their mother lights the lamp.
I walked down the quiet lane and listened to the rain falling on the roof of the cottage.
The sailor often thinks about his home, his family and the fields he left behind.
A small bird sat on the branch and sang, even though the woods were already bare.
The young women danced in the meadow under the willow until it got dark.
In the evening the farm workers rested and talked about the harvests of past years.
I felt numb for months, and only in spring did I start to feel like myself again.

notes: Card: no dominant token; the top examples are function and content words inside old-fashioned verse lines (A romping on the green; dead and gone; a crumb - of me), plus a few digits in years and zip codes. Near misses say the same thing as plain prose.
